new_statements.rule_in_words: Smythe assigns 'final' as the main position of accent to his whole Group 3 (Manus and adjacent islands, some 25 languages), which includes Levei and Drehet; this is a group-level table cell, not a description of Khehek. Blust's 1975 Ndrehet field transcriptions (RB2-011 pp.285-295, held by the project) mark stress overwhelmingly on the initial syllable (penult in disyllables, antepenult in trisyllables), with final marks mainly on glottal-final or 3sg-suffixed forms, so the only primary evidence points the other way.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing in Smythe. Blust's Ndrehet notes occasionally write a grave (secondary) on a later syllable, e.g. púrikòhuN.
new_statements.exceptions: None in Smythe (table cell only; 'tones: + in some dialects' for Group 3).
new_statements.domain_note: Smythe: unspecified (impressionistic group typology). Blust fieldnotes: isolated citation forms elicited from one teenage speaker per variety.
new_statements.identity_note: kheh1237 Khehek = Levei + Drehet (Ndrehet) [+ Bucho/Pujou] of west-central Manus; older sources (Smythe 1970, Schooling 1988, Ross 1988) fold it into 'Levei-Tulu (Keli)', whose Tulu half is now Tulu-Bohuai (tulu1259, ISO rak). Blust's packets are village-specific: packet 8 = Levei dialect, packet 19 = Ndrehet (Drehet) dialect. Smythe's accent cell is for his entire Group 3 (all Manus languages), not for Khehek.

sources.note: Levei (8.5 h) and Drehet (4.25 h) are in Table 0.1 of survey languages but are NOT among the eight sketched; they appear only in numeral/lexical comparisons. Nearest sister-language statement is sketch 5 Likum sec. 5.2 (stress 'relatively even on the penultimate and final syllables.. transcribed as uniformly penultimate'). Nothing on Levei/Drehet stress.

sources.note: PRIMARY DATA ONLY, no prose. Handwritten phonetic transcriptions carry frequent acute stress marks, overwhelmingly on the FIRST syllable (lúEh 'two', túloh, háhup, límEh, rúnoh, lúNoh, kámop, pélE, khámak, káwah, ásap, sóhaN, kénEp, kúih; trisyllables+ ká?acuk, kólohop, núkupuN, kápwililih, púrikòhuN with grave secondary); final marks mostly on glottal-final or 3sg-suffixed forms (pEcé?, mEté?, nEcité?, matáN, ná?aN, upwiséh).
